# About This Script

In this section, we will evaluate the trait-environment using a Community Weighted Mean significance test (CWM.sig) based on permutations. Two permutational approach are considered here:

- site.shuffle: performs permutations of CWM values across sites to evaluate the relationship between CWM and environmental variables using an ordinary least squares (OLS) regression;

- trait.shuffle: permutes species trait values within the species pool, recalculates null CWM values, and links them to environmental gradients via OLS.

We have used 9,999 permutations in this process.

The output of this script will be a supplement for Table 1 and Appendix S11.

# Packages 

The packages required to this section are bellow, most of
them are available on CRAN. The CWM.sig function is available in [Duarte et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2081).


```{r}
rm(list = ls()) ## Clear the R environment to ensure a clean workspace
gc()

library(here)            # To establish the path context
library(SYNCSA)          # For ecological analysis, includes CWM and null models
library(openxlsx)        # Reading/writing Excel files
source(here("func/cwm_sig.txt"))         # Custom function for CWM significance testing
source(here("func/summarize_trees.R"))   # Custom script, possibly for summarizing phylogenetic trees
library(tidyverse)       # For data manipulation and visualization
library(readxl)          # Reading Excel files


runs = 9999              # Number of permutations for the null model
options(scipen = 9999)   # Avoid scientific notation in outputs
```

# Load data 

We will push into this script the organized data produced in the step *1.2-Eval_Spatial_Correlation_TRAW.qmd*.

```{r}
org_data <- readRDS(file = here("data/org_data.RDS"))    

```

# Load models
We will also load the models and intermediary steps to verify if we are reproducing the models correctly. 

```{r}
nice_mods <- read.xlsx(here('outputs/cwm_raw_results.xlsx'), sheet = 3) # List of relevant models
cwm_values <- readRDS(here("data/cwm_values_raw.RDS"))                  # Raw CWM values
```

# CWM SIG Testing

Now we will test each trait against environmental predictors using the permutation-based null models.

```{r}
nice_mods

rdiam <- get_cwm(
  comm = org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = diam ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + samp_size + plot_size,
  runs = runs,
  model = T
)

rcomp <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = r_comp ~ nitrogen + cec + samp_size + plot_size,
  runs = runs
)

screep <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = r_cr ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

lcreep <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = r_lr ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

lmseg <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = lmseg ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

ind <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = ind ~ prec_warm + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

dim <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = ldim ~ prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  runs = runs
)

spore <- get_cwm(
  org_data$community,
  trait = org_data$traits,
  env = org_data$environmental,
  formula = chl ~
    ann_prec *
      prec_seas +
      plot_size +
      samp_size,
  runs = runs
)
```

## Output data 

Here we will combine all CWM significance results into a single data frame. This dataframe will be supplement for Table 1 and Appendix S11.

```{r}
cwm.results <-
  full_join(rcomp$cwm.sig, screep$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(lcreep$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(rdiam$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(lmseg$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(ind$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(dim$cwm.sig) %>%
  full_join(spore$cwm.sig)

# View only significant results (p-value < 0.05)
cwm.results[cwm.results$ts < 0.05, ]

# Combine model data for further plotting or correlation analysis
p <- cbind(
  rdiam$model$data,
  rcomp$model$data,
  screep$model$data,
  lmseg$model$data,
  ind$model$data,
  dim$model$data,
  spore$model$data
)

# Remove duplicated columns
df <- p[!duplicated(as.list(p))]

# Example correlation between two traits
cor_cwm <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(df[,c(1, 12:18)]))
corrplot::corrplot(cor_cwm$r,
         type = "upper",
         p.mat = cor_cwm$P,
         sig.level = 0.05,
         method = 'number',
         insig = "blank")  
str(df)

```

## Save data

```{r}
write.xlsx(
  x = list(results = cwm.results, plots = df),     # Save both results and model data
here("outputs/cwm_sig_traw.xlsx"),                     # Output path
  startRow = 1,
  startCol = 1,
  keepNA = T,                                       # Keep missing values
  rowNames = T                                      # Include row names
)
```
